nodes.title: PROMPT A — independent comparison
widgets_values:
Image 1 is the primary geometry constraint reference.
Image 2 defines the transparent PC material language.
Image 3 defines the PISCIS visual identity and knob morphology.
Image 4 defines the fader and switch design language.
Image 5 provides secondary product-detail inspiration.
Image 6 provides flat panel-graphics inspiration.

Create a compact front-facing musical control module concept.

Hard constraints:
- preserve the overall product proportion and front-view composition from Image 1
- preserve the compact upright rectangular format
- preserve the clear separation of upper control region and lower performance region
- preserve a dense, integrated, highly compact panel architecture

Soft constraints:
- reinterpret all details rather than copying literally
- merge all reference cues into one unified industrial design language
- maintain a premium consumer-electronics appearance

Use Image 2 for CMF:
translucent / transparent PC shell, frosted clear plastic, light body, dark control parts, subtle visibility of internal construction.

Use Image 3 for style:
PISCIS-like graphic balance, playful precision, exposed screws, clean knob cluster, strong faceplate color block, friendly but premium visual identity.

Use Image 3 for knob design:
simple cylindrical rotary knobs, rounded edges, tactile proportions, subtle pointer indication, one accent knob among neutral knobs.

Use Image 4 for control language:
integrate compact vertical faders and small switches in a neat aligned composition.

Use Image 5 for detail refinement:
slim packaging, precise edge treatment, compact product-object quality.

Use Image 6 for panel graphics:
flat UI-like graphics, clean legends, subtle grouped visual language, soft modern interface aesthetics.

The final design must feel:
compact, premium, translucent, graphic, coherent, and highly intentional.

Avoid:
generic synthesizer clutter,
messy control distribution,
bulky housing,
heavy retro styling,
overly mechanical visual noise,
literal copying of the reference images.

Clean studio render, front view, high detail, industrial design presentation.

nodes.title: PROMPT B — independent comparison
widgets_values:
Image 1 is the geometry reference.
Image 2 is the transparent CMF reference.
Image 3 is the PISCIS styling and knob reference.
Image 4 is a hard layout requirement reference for the fader bank.
Image 5 is a detail refinement reference.
Image 6 is a panel graphics reference.

Design a compact premium PISCIS-style musical control module.

Preserve:
- upright rectangular front view
- lower dense button matrix
- 6 large rotary knobs

Mandatory:
- include 5 vertical faders
- include 4 small switches above the faders
- the faders must be clearly visible
- do not omit the faders
- do not replace the faders with knobs

Use translucent frosted PC plastic, exposed corner screws, rounded tactile knobs, clean modern UI-like graphics, and a compact highly integrated layout.

The panel must clearly contain three control groups:
1. 6 knobs
2. 5 faders + 4 switches
3. button matrix

Front view, clean studio render, high detail.

nodes.title: PROMPT C — independent comparison
widgets_values:
Image 1 is the absolute geometry and mask-edit boundary. Keep the ENTIRE lower button matrix, external enclosure proportions, screws, visual framing and strict orthographic top view unchanged. Redesign ONLY the masked upper surface. One unified PISCIS LAB instrument, unchanged footprint.

Exactly SIX thin recessed rotary controls, FIVE compact sliding faders, and FOUR tiny tactile switches; 15 total and all functionally plausible, legible and accessible. Avoid tall rotary knobs and separate modules.

Image 2: smoked blue semitransparent injection-molded polycarbonate and ultra-shallow mechanical layers. Image 3: original PISCIS DNA and creamy white + subtle yellow hardware. Image 4: mechanically believable faders/switches. Image 5 and 6: interpret their material, surface rhythm and detail language, but do NOT transfer their enclosure, geometry, scale, function or camera angle.

DIRECTION C — ASYMMETRIC SCULPTURAL PRECISION. Investigate an unexpectedly sophisticated asymmetrical arrangement: a sweeping compact arrangement of flat miniature rotary discs interlocked with recessed linear slider zones; a reserved narrow switch bank; expressive negative space and hierarchy; non-uniform but logical micro-clusters; translucent blue layered surfaces and elegant clean typography. Radical but manufacturable and usable, extremely compact yet premium. Keep every control within the original upper-panel region, and retain the entire lower section and outside framing. White studio background, exact top-down orthographic single-product concept render.

nodes.title: Read me — 3 prompts / 6 shared references
widgets_values:
# FLUX.2 Klein — 3-prompt comparison / 6 image references

- Input 1 = locked geometry, 2–6 = style / components / materials. **Replace image 5 and image 6 before running**.
- Edit the large `PROMPT A`, `PROMPT B`, `PROMPT C` text boxes independently. Same 6 reference images + same initial fixed seed for controlled comparisons.
- One shared mask defines **WHITE = upper panel to redraw** and **BLACK = preserve**; align it with reference image 1.
- Sampling geometry **384 × 480**; final PNG saved via `OUTPUT A/B/C` at **320 × 400** to reduce disk usage and preview size.
- The external VAEEncode -> SetLatentNoiseMask supplies all three branches, avoids the original cycle, then ImageCompositeMasked restores unmasked pixels directly from Image 1.
- When changing output resolution, keep the 6 reference ImageScale nodes, mask ImageScale, and final output scale nodes consistent.
- Prompt A retains your full previous detailed wording. B and C introduce compact, differentiated design directions.
